intro: The WAKers is a training lab with two programs, cancer and neuroscience. Students and early-career researchers do real projects on either side, from designing experiments to writing the paper.

positions.title: Graduate students
positions.text: Thesis projects through AUB's graduate programs in the Faculty of Medicine.

positions.title: Medical students
positions.text: Research electives and longer projects alongside medical training.

positions.title: Research assistants
positions.who: Graduates in biology or related fields
positions.text: Full-time positions supporting projects, when funding allows.

positions.title: Postdoctoral fellows
positions.text: Independent projects in organoids, cancer stem cells or neurogenesis.

positions.title: Undergraduates and summer students
positions.text: Short projects and hands-on experience in a working lab.

skills: Animal models of cancer and brain injury

steps.title: Read our work
steps.text: Look through our two research programs and a few recent papers to see which side fits your interests.

steps.title: Email Dr. Abou-Kheir
steps.text: Send your CV, your program and year, and two or three sentences on what you'd like to work on, and whether you lean towards the cancer or the neuroscience side.

steps.title: Meet the team
steps.text: If there's a good fit, you'll be invited to meet the lab and discuss a project.
